Computational biologist and senior scientist in Translational Medicine at Orion Pharma, Finland. Supports oncology research across pre-clinical and clinical programmes, with recent focus on immuno-oncology bioinformatics, indication selection, and biomarker discovery using patient molecular data.

**Contact:** [nelkibs@gmail.com](mailto:nelkibs@gmail.com) · [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/nelson-kibinge-1b1477223/) · [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=0aNS07IAAAAJ&hl=en&oi=ao) · [GitHub](https://github.com/nelkibs)

## Current focus and strengths

- Clinical-project support, including indication selection and translational decision-making through integration of disease biology with clinical and molecular evidence.
- Biomarker discovery and evaluation using patient DNA sequencing, circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA), and RNA sequencing data.
- Immuno-oncology bioinformatics: tumour–immune biology, immune-cell populations, tumour-infiltrating immune cells, and molecular signatures.
- Multi-omics integration across genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, single-cell, and spatial data.
- R and Python tool development, reusable analytical workflows, and Shiny applications for research and development.
- AI-enabled approaches for oncology target discovery and prioritization, target-confidence assessment, and hypothesis generation.
- Cross-functional collaboration across translational, clinical, computational, and experimental teams; clear communication of analytical findings.

## Professional experience

### Senior Scientist – Computational Biologist | Orion Pharma

**February 2020–Present · Turku, Finland**

Works in Translational Medicine, supporting oncology research and development. Develops and applies computational approaches to high-throughput omics data, contributes to target prioritization and biomarker discovery, develops data-science tools, and supports data-driven bioinformatics and AI collaborations.

### Senior Research Associate – Statistical Genomics | MRC Integrative Epidemiology Unit, University of Bristol

**April 2019–January 2020 · Bristol, United Kingdom**

Applied genomics and epidemiology methods to identify therapeutic targets for autoimmune diseases, communicated scientific findings, and facilitated academic–pharma collaboration.

### Visiting Research Scientist | Heidelberg University

**January–March 2019 · Heidelberg, Germany**

Developed statistical methods for analysis of KILchip Protein Microarray data.

### Senior Postdoctoral Scientist – Acting Head of Statistics | KEMRI-Wellcome Trust Research Programme

**March 2018–June 2019 · Kilifi, Kenya**

Led the statistics unit, supported institutional statistical needs, and developed statistical methods for diverse omics datasets.

### Early Career Postdoctoral Scientist | KEMRI-Wellcome Trust Research Programme

**March 2016–November 2018 · Kilifi, Kenya**

Conducted research on malaria and virus genomics and diversity in long-term surveillance; published research; and supervised master’s students and interns.

### Adjunct Faculty | Pwani University

**July 2016–Present · Kilifi, Kenya**

Taught MSc Bioinformatics courses in biostatistics, data science for biology, databases, and data visualization; examines master’s and doctoral theses in bioinformatics.

### Bioinformatics Intern | Yukiguni Maitake

**March–September 2015 · Niigata, Japan**

Developed transcriptomics and genomics software tools supporting research and development in Maitake mushroom cultivation.

### Medical Sales Representative | Pharmaken Kenya Ltd.

**2008–2009 · Kenya**

Marketed generic anti-inflammatory and analgesic products in Nairobi and the North Eastern region.
